title: PR Night Notes: Heuristic Bento
content:
Late-night, half-sober review notes. Use this like a compact bento: small, compartmentalized checks that I can run quickly before merging refactors. Not polished — personal mental checklist + commands + small hypothesis list.

Goal
- Reduce merge friction for medium-risk refactors (kv-cache, batching, route-sanitization) without blocking on perfect design. Establish an order of quick-safety checks that give 80% confidence in 20% of the time.

Heuristic Bento (4 compartments)
1) Smoke & correctness (top-left)
  - Run the focused unit/integration smoke for touched modules. Prioritize end-to-end happy path.
  - Quick examples:
    * endpoints: curl -sS -X POST $LOCAL_HOST/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' | jq -r '.text'
    * kv cache: run local KV debug util: python tools/kv_debug.py --check-sanity
  - Red flags: failing smoke, large diffs in serializing/shape code, changed default feature flags.

2) Performance sanity (top-right)
  - Check that no obvious hotspot introduced (locking, linear scan, repeated allocs).
  - Local perf quick:
    * pprof flame: run small load harness (10 qps, seq len 64) and compare flame graphs
    * simple bench: go test ./pkg/serve -bench BenchmarkServeSmall -run none -benchmem
  - Flags: added sync.WaitGroup in hot loop, new allocation per token, new map ops per request.

3) API/contract invariants (bottom-left)
  - Validate public API shape (request/response keys), backwards-compatible defaults.
  - Tests: contract test suite: scripts/run_contract_tests.sh --endpoints changed
  - Look for: renames of fields, removed optional fields, changed error codes.

4) Ops & deploy resilience (bottom-right)
  - Can we rollout with canary? Is there an automatic fallback? Check rollout config.
  - Quick checks: CI deploy job passes for dedicated images; dockerfile changes; config flags wired for runtime fallbacks.
  - Red flag: new env var without default, added required secret, hard-coded region.

Quick review script (my mental checklist)
- Read PR title + first 3 comments for intent. Anything ambiguous -> comment asking for user story.
- Scan files changed: grouping by module. If >4 modules touched, escalate to small design sync.
- For each file: what is the runtime cost of this change (allocs, locks, syscalls)?
- Run unit tests locally for touched packages: make test PKG=./pkg/serve TEST=short
- Run focused integration: docker-compose up --build --abort-on-container-exit; watch logs for 30s.
- Run linter + static analyzers: make lint-fast
- If change touches caching/kv/batching: run memory profile with small harness.

Commands I use a lot (copy-paste)
- git checkout -b reviewer/PR-2148 && git fetch origin pull/2148/head && git reset --hard FETCH_HEAD
- make test PKG=./pkg/cache TEST=short
- ./scripts/load_harness --qps=10 --seq=64 --duration=30s --target=http://localhost:8080
- python tools/kv_debug.py --stats | jq .cache_hit_rate
- curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/rerank -d @testdata/re-rank-req.json | jq .

Refactor safety patterns (quick heuristics)
- Prefer additive changes: deprecate flag but keep old behavior until next major.
- If moving code across packages, ensure internal invariants tested (round-trip tests).
- Small commits: prefer 5-10 file commits for visibility rather than 100+ file rebases.
- If touching serialization, include cross-version round-trip test (old->new->old).

Roll-forward vs rollback approach
- If ambiguous risk, prefer roll-forward with feature flag and narrow canary (1% traffic) and automated regression detection (latency + error spikes).
- Immediate rollback if: error rate > 5x baseline OR 30% increase p95 latency for 10m.

Follow-ups (todo)
- Add a small harness under infra/test-harness that can run the 4-bento checks automatically against a PR branch. Ticket: INF-987.
- Extract common perf guard rails in a README for reviewers (short checklist + commands).
- Add a lightweight CI job (bento-check) that runs smoke + contract tests + quick perf baseline (5s bench).

Hypotheses to validate later
- Small, targeted perf microbenchmarks catch 70% of regressions we see in canary. (Need data)
- Most user-visible regressions stem from changed default flags or missing fallbacks.

Notes to self (stream-of-consciousness)
- Avoid deep-dive unless PR touches critical path (serve/runtime/hotloop). If it does, allocate 1hr paired review with author.
- When in doubt, ask for a short recording of the change: one-min narrated run-through in PR description helps a lot.
- Remember: code readability > clever micro-optimizations on first pass; prefer follow-up perf PR over risky inline micro-ops in merge.

Done-for-now markers
- If all bento compartments green, leave a +1 with the checklist bullet points. If any red flags -> block and request a patch with tests/mitigations.

End of notes.

Recent quick references for this PR run:
- Observed: tiny perf blip when kv cache hit metric dropped by 6% on canary (02/08). Might be related to change in LRU eviction order.
- TODO: ask author for benchmark harness command used in PR and full flame graph.

---
Personal signature: Aditi (review nights: prefer terse PR descriptions, explicit migration steps, and one-line perf summary).
